- Moreover, being a predictive group-contribution method, UNIFAC does not require experimental binary interaction parame-ters�which are unavailable for this system�making it well suited here.^31,44 Hybrid approaches such as the Predictive Soave−Redlich−Kwong (PSRK) model combine a cubic equation of state with a group-contribution activity-coefficient model and are typically employed for higher-pressure systems and where binary interaction parameters are unavailable.^37,38 Because the stripper operates near atmospheric pressure, where vapor-phase nonideality is negligible, the added complexity of a predictive equation of state is not warranted, and a direct activity-coefficient description of the liquid phase was preferred.
- High efficiency in the separation of isoprene from the feed gas was demonstrated by the absorption column, with 97% of the isoprene being recovered into the solvent.
- Simultaneously, 99.8% of the air and 98% of the CO2 were removed.
- To achieve this separation, a solvent-to-feed gas ratio of 1.2 was required.
- However, through effective recycling, net solvent loss was minimized to only 15 g kg^− 1 isoprene, highlighting the sustainability of the process.
- It was found that the lowest energy requirement per kilogram of isoprene occurred at 2 °C. At lower temperatures, isoprene absorption efficiency was markedly increased.

The energy demand per kg of isoprene rose as the feed isoprene concentration increased because the process required more energy to recover isoprene from the feed gas at higher concentrations. The energy demand is affected by the concentration of isoprene in the feed gas, with higher concentrations requiring more energy to separate and recover the isoprene.
